2. Layoffs Over Time

Monthly count of layoff events and total employees affected. The 2022–2023 period saw the largest waves, driven by post-pandemic corrections in the tech sector.

3. Geographical Distribution

The United States dominates the dataset, accounting for nearly two-thirds of all recorded layoff events. India, Canada, the UK, and Israel round out the top five.

4. Geographic Evolution Over Time

The animated map below shows how layoffs spread geographically year by year. Use the slider to navigate across years.
The stacked area charts below compare US layoffs to the rest of the world. While the US consistently leads in absolute numbers, non-US layoffs have been growing as a share over time.

4b. US Deep Dive: State & City Heatmaps

Zooming into the United States, California dominates overwhelmingly — largely driven by the SF Bay Area — followed by New York and Washington state.
The heatmaps below show how layoffs concentrate in major tech hubs, with the SF Bay Area consistently leading by a wide margin across all years.

5. Industry Breakdown

Finance, Retail, and Healthcare lead in event count. However, Retail and Transportation dominate in total headcount, reflecting larger layoff events at major employers.
The heatmap below shows industry-level layoff totals by year. The 2023 peak is visible across nearly all sectors.

6. Company Stage & Funding

Post-IPO companies account for the largest share of layoff events and by far the largest average layoff size, reflecting the scale of publicly traded tech firms.
